title: Sell Mineral Rights in Lloydsville, OH
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Lloydsville, OH | Belmont County
metaDescription: Lloydsville sits in Belmont County's Utica core, near heavy horizontal drilling. Learn how nearby unit activity shapes an offer on your mineral interest.
heroLead: Lloydsville is a small unincorporated community in Belmont County, in the thick part of the Utica/Point Pleasant core, where more horizontal wells have been drilled per square mile than almost anywhere else in Ohio.
intro: Belmont County has been ground zero for Ohio's Utica shale development since the play took off, and Lloydsville sits well within that core. If your mineral interest is anywhere near here, there's a real chance it's already inside a producing drilling unit, already leased, or at minimum close enough to active pads that a buyer can value it against real production numbers instead of guesswork.

sections.heading: What being inside a Belmont County core unit means
paragraphs: Operators active in this part of Belmont County over the years have included names like Gulfport Energy, Ascent Resources, and more recently Encino Energy, which picked up a large chunk of legacy acreage. If your tract near Lloydsville is inside one of their drilling units, you should be receiving a division order and periodic royalty statements. Those statements are actually the best evidence a buyer can use to value your interest, because they show real production and real decline, not projected numbers.

sections.heading: If you're already receiving royalty checks
paragraphs: Selling a producing mineral interest is a different conversation than selling an unleased one. Buyers value producing interests off the decline curve: how much the well is making now, how fast that number is dropping month over month, and how many years of remaining production the well likely has left. Bring your last several royalty statements to that conversation; they tell the story faster than anything else.

sections.heading: Checking Belmont County records for lease and unit status
paragraphs: The Belmont County Recorder's office in St. Clairsville keeps the lease and unit designation filings for this area. Before selling, confirm which unit your tract sits in, who currently operates it, and whether your lease has any special provisions like a pugh clause that would affect what happens to unleased portions of a larger tract.

sections.heading: Old family tracts near Lloydsville
paragraphs: A lot of the land around Lloydsville has stayed in the same families since well before the shale era, farmed or timbered rather than developed. That history means mineral ownership records sometimes lag behind current family structure, so before a sale can close cleanly, a title check confirming exactly who the current legal owners are, and in what percentages, is usually the first real step.

faqs.question: Is Lloydsville a good location for mineral rights value?
faqs.answer: It sits in the thick core of the Utica/Point Pleasant play in Belmont County, which has seen heavy horizontal drilling. Whether a specific tract is valuable depends on whether it's inside a producing unit, but the surrounding activity level is real.

faqs.question: Who operates wells near Lloydsville?
faqs.answer: Belmont County has had activity from several operators over the years, including Gulfport Energy and Ascent Resources, with Encino Energy now holding a large amount of legacy acreage. Your division order will show the current operator for your specific unit.

faqs.question: How does an operator change affect my mineral rights?
faqs.answer: When one company sells acreage to another, your lease terms generally carry over unchanged; only the operator name on your royalty statement changes. Check that your latest statement matches the current operator of record.

faqs.question: What should I bring to value a producing interest?
faqs.answer: Your last six to twelve months of royalty statements are the most useful documents, since they show actual production and decline rather than estimates.
